data.habitat_ai: Infrequently in deciduous forests, valleys on acidic loess soils with good drainage; disturbed sites including stream banks, rocky slopes, cliff edges in mountainous regions like Tianmu Mountains, southeastern China.
data.ecological_function_ai: Pioneer species in disturbed environments via clonal reproduction and sprouting from basal lignotubers; stabilizes eroded slopes; provides habitat for birds and food via seeds; resilient in low-density mixed forests.
data.native_adapted_habitats_ai: Native to southeastern China (e.g., Zhejiang, Tianmu Mountains); adapted to temperate deciduous/mixed broadleaf forests, urban environments, pollution-tolerant worldwide.
data.agroforestry_use_cases_ai: Fruit (seed) production for edible nuts (ginnan) and medicinal uses in China; leaf extracts for pharmaceuticals; urban street trees; limited timber; agroforestry plantations in China for nuts and leaves.
data.general_description_ai: Ginkgo biloba is the sole surviving species of Ginkgoales, a gymnosperm tree native to East Asia. Long-lived (up to 3500+ years), disease- and pest-resistant, dioecious with unique fan-shaped leaves turning bright yellow in autumn. Grows 20-50m tall, deep-rooted, capable of clonal reproduction via basal sprouts and aerial roots.
data.compatible_soil_types_ai: Well-drained sandy, loamy, or silty (loess) soils; pH 5.0-8.0; tolerates poor, compacted, alkaline, urban polluted, and salty soils.
data.growth_form_ai: Deciduous gymnosperm tree; pyramidal/conical when young, developing broad, irregular, angular crown with age; deep-rooted, wind- and snow-resistant; short spur shoots and long shoots.
data.leaf_type_ai: Fan-shaped, 5-10 cm (up to 15 cm) long, leathery, with dichotomous venation; alternate on long shoots, clustered on spur shoots; bright green turning golden yellow in fall.
data.flower_color_ai: Inconspicuous; greenish-yellow (male pollen cones/catkins), cream/tan-green (female ovules)
data.fruit_type_ai: Fleshy-coated naked seeds (sarcotesta), 1.5-2 cm, plum-like, yellow-brown, foul-smelling (butyric acid) when ripe; hard sclerotesta shell enclosing edible gametophyte nut.
data.bark_characteristics_ai: Light gray to gray-brown, deeply furrowed with irregular ridges and furrows; corky, fire-resistant.
data.stewardship_best_practices_ai: Full sun exposure; well-drained soil; moderate water until established, then drought-tolerant; highly resilient to urban stress, pollution, salt; prefer male cultivars to avoid messy fruit.
data.planting_recipes_ai: Plant in spring or fall; full sun, well-drained site; space 10-15 m apart; transplant balled-and-burlapped or container; mulch base; select grafted male clones for urban/ornamental use.
data.pruning_maintenance_ai: Minimal required; formative pruning in late winter during youth to develop central leader and structure; remove dead/weak branches; tolerates heavy pruning.
data.disease_pest_management_ai: Highly resistant to diseases and pests; minor issues include aphids, spider mites, seed bugs (on females); manage with insecticidal soap or horticultural oil if needed; rarely problematic.
data.fire_management_ai: Fire-resistant with low flammability, thick bark secreting retardant sap; survives low-intensity fires via resprouting; second lowest flammability among deciduous trees.
data.cultural_significance_ai: Symbol of longevity, resilience, peace in Chinese, Japanese, Korean cultures; sacred tree planted at temples since 14th century; medicinal uses (leaves/seeds) for 1000+ years; official tree of Tokyo; ginkgo leaf icons in universities, tea ceremony.
